scientific_summary: The source-defined synthetic EAEYEHL peptide was administered as Myoki/CG-A1 with arginine and maltodextrin, nominally 200 mg/day orally for 12 weeks, versus the named background ingredients without peptide. Eighty adults with muscle atrophy were randomized 40/40; the outcome table reports 38 Myoki/37 placebo analyzed, while the native flowchart reverses the arm labels. The primary DEXA lean-mass comparison favors Myoki by 705.8 g (95% CI 433.40–978.16). Authors report adjusted secondary contrasts of −0.34 seconds for a six-metre walk (−0.68–0.00; P<.01), +0.27 kg left grip (−0.15–0.69; P=.02) and +0.43 kg right grip (−0.04–0.89; P=.04). Retain these actual comparative estimates without repairing their inconsistent confidence intervals/P values or treating them as proven nulls. Per-protocol exclusions, including inadequate efficacy, multiplicity, unresolved shared-ingredient quantities and copied comparator-dose wording limit inference. Four biomarker comparisons were nonsignificant; registered troponin I was unreported. Mild TEAEs affected 10/40 versus 7/40 as stated in the main, without a demonstrated comparative safety conclusion. Cell interaction with myostatin is not receptor blockade or human target engagement; mouse histology lacks direct physiological function. Current registry timing, unavailable historical analysis plan and sponsor disclosures remain qualified. Marketed-product identity, oral bioavailability, useful durable function, renewal and chromosome fidelity are unestablished. Apply the same criteria as the provisional compensation nominee; no MVA, BUBR1-restoration or superiority claim follows.
